issues.description: The problem text instructs students to initialize the SealSaloon's stock in the constructor as a normal (instance) final field, but later explicitly requires the stock attribute to be static (shared across all instances). This is a contradiction: a static final field cannot be properly initialized per-instance in the constructor. Students will be confused whether to implement a per-instance final stock set in the constructor or a static final stock initialized at declaration.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the specification: decide whether stock is an instance final field initialized in the constructor or a static final shared field. If the intent is a shared stock, update the earlier instruction to initialize the static final stock at declaration (or in a static initializer) and remove the guidance to initialize it in the instance constructor. If the intent is per-instance stock, remove the requirement that stock be static.

issues.description: The UML/problem shows acceptSupplyDelivery as a public (+) method, but the reference implementation declares acceptSupplyDelivery as package-private static (no public modifier). This visibility mismatch can confuse students about the required method visibility and may cause tests or external callers to be unable to access the method if they expect it to be public.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification and reference implementation consistent. Preferably declare acceptSupplyDelivery as public static in the solution (add the public modifier) to match the UML and problem text, or update the UML/text to indicate package-private if that is intentional.
